mainTopic: רבי עקיבא's 'stolen answer' and רבי יוחנן's rebuttal of ריש לקיש; the משנה on how sprinkling the blood makes the laws of קדשי קדשים and קדשים קלים more lenient or more strict
overview: The amud opens by finishing רבי עקיבא's קל וחומר. If sprinkling one חטאת's blood frees even the unfit partner animal from מעילה, it should surely free its own meat that left the עזרה. ריש לקיש, quoting רב אושעיא, calls this a 'stolen answer': the premise only holds when both animals were slaughtered together, and he argues the timing should not matter. רבי יוחנן challenges him with a case of two backup אשמות and עולא's rule about parts put on the altar too early. That case shows animals slaughtered one after the other count as separate bodies, and ריש לקיש is left silent. A new משנה then teaches that sprinkling the blood of קדשי קדשים is both lenient and strict, while for קדשים קלים it is only strict. The גמרא asks why the משנה's wording 'אין מועלין בבשר' seems to leave an איסור on meat that belongs to the כהנים or the owners. For קדשי קדשים it answers that the wording just matches the רישא. For קדשים קלים, רבי חנינא explains that the משנה is talking about meat that went out, following רבי עקיבא. He begins to explain that רבי עקיבא's 'sprinkling works' concerns the burning of such meat, and this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's premise: one sprinkling frees both animals
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא gets his student to agree that sprinkling the blood of one חטאת frees both its own meat and the meat of its 'partner' animal from מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the blood of one of the two animals was sprinkled, don't you agree that just as its blood frees its own meat from מעילה, it also frees the meat of the other animal from מעילה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא is laying down a starting point that his student must accept. This sets up the קל וחומר that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case has two חטאת animals: one that was lost and the replacement set aside in its place. רבי עקיבא says that sprinkling the blood of one of them frees the meat of both from מעילה. Once the student accepts this, רבי עקיבא can build his argument on it.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition against using or benefiting from הקדש (holy property); breaking it requires a קרבן and repayment
The blood was sprinkled on the מזבח, the key act that completes the offering
Exempts, frees from a law
Its partner, meaning the other animal in the pair

phrases.english: If the blood of one of them was sprinkled,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the two חטאת animals in the case just before this: the lost one and the one set aside to replace it.

phrases.english: do you not agree

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכְּשֵׁם שֶׁדָּמָהּ פּוֹטֵר אֶת בְּשָׂרָהּ מִן הַמְּעִילָה,
phrases.english: that just as its blood frees its own meat from misuse,

phrases.aramaic: אַף יִפְטוֹר בְּשַׂר חֲבֶירְתָּהּ מִן הַמְּעִילָה?
phrases.english: it also frees the meat of its partner from misuse?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי עקיבא's argument from the case of the lost and replaced חטאת, which comes just before this.
steps.raayaObject: That זריקה removes מעילה from meat even when the meat itself has a problem
steps.raayaSupportSource: The agreed case of two חטאת animals, where one sprinkling frees both

steps.title: The קל וחומר: surely it frees its own meat
steps.stepSummary: If sprinkling saves even the other animal's unfit meat from מעילה, it should certainly save its own meat, even if that meat left the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the sprinkling saved the other animal's meat from מעילה, even though that animal is unfit, it is only logical that it saves its own meat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא completes his קל וחומר. He concludes that sprinkling frees the meat that left the עזרה from מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other animal is פסול, since it is a leftover חטאת that will never be offered, yet the sprinkling still helps it. The meat that left the courtyard belongs to the very animal whose blood was sprinkled, so it is closer to the sprinkling and should be helped even more.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a weaker case to a stronger one; here hinted at by the words דין הוא
Saved, rescued (here: from מעילה)
Unfit for the מזבח
'It is only logical', the opening words of a conclusion reached by reasoning

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא's position: once the blood is sprinkled, there is no מעילה on the meat, even meat that left the עזרה, and he proves it with a קל וחומר from the extra חטאת.

phrases.aramaic: אִם הִצִּיל בְּשַׂר חֲבֶירְתָּהּ מִן הַמְּעִילָה,
phrases.english: If it saved the meat of its partner from misuse,
even though that one is unfit,
phrases.notes: The partner animal is unfit because it is an extra חטאת that will never be brought.

phrases.english: it is only logical that it should save its own meat!
phrases.notes: 'Its own meat' here is the meat that went out of the courtyard before the blood was sprinkled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds the קל וחומר on the premise agreed to in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That meat which left the עזרה is freed from מעילה by זריקה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the unfit partner animal in step 1

steps.title: ריש לקיש: רבי עקיבא's answer was deceptive
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש, quoting רב אושעיא, says רבי עקיבא gave his student a 'stolen' answer, because his premise implies that it works only when both animals were slaughtered together, a distinction ריש לקיש rejects.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said in the name of רב אושעיא: רבי עקיבא gave that student a deceptive answer. If the animals were slaughtered at the same time, yes, the sprinkling frees the other. If they were slaughtered one after the other, no.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש attacks רבי עקיבא's proof. He says its starting point does not hold in every case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The premise in step 1 sounded general, but ריש לקיש points out that רבי עקיבא's answer implies it only works when both animals were slaughtered at the same moment, and not one after the other. ריש לקיש himself rejects that distinction, so the answer leaned on a split he considers baseless, which is why he calls the answer 'stolen'.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'stolen' answer: one that sounds convincing but hides a weakness
At the same time
One after the other
Yes / no (Aramaic)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Stolen' does not mean רבי עקיבא lied. It means his answer worked by quietly assuming a narrow case.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said in the name of Rav Oshaya:
Rabbi Akiva gave a deceptive answer
to that student,
phrases.notes: The student he was arguing with is רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: if they were slaughtered at the same time, yes,
phrases.notes: The word 'slaughtered' is not in the text; the גמרא assumes it. 'Yes' means the sprinkling does free the other animal.

phrases.english: if one after the other, no,

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּשׁוּבָה גְּנוּבָה הֱשִׁיבוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְאוֹתוֹ תַּלְמִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Criticizes the premise on which רבי עקיבא's קל וחומר was built.
steps.kashyaTarget: The premise in step 1 that one sprinkling always frees the partner animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The premise is only true when both animals were slaughtered at once, so the proof rests on a narrow case presented as if it were general.

steps.title: Why should the timing of the slaughter matter?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש continues and explains his complaint: since the other animal is unfit in either case, why should it matter whether they were slaughtered together or one after the other?
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it is unfit either way, what difference does it make to me whether they were slaughtered at the same time or one after the other?
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש is still speaking. He explains why רבי עקיבא's answer was 'stolen': the distinction it relies on, slaughtered together versus one after the other, should not matter at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the second animal is a leftover, unfit חטאת. ריש לקיש's own view is that the timing makes no difference. That is why he calls רבי עקיבא's answer 'stolen': it only worked by leaning on a distinction ריש לקיש rejects. The next step shows רבי יוחנן challenging him on this.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because
'What is it to me?', meaning what difference does it make

phrases.english: For since it is unfit,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the other animal, whose blood was not sprinkled.

phrases.english: what difference is it to me whether at the same time,
or one after the other?!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכֵיוָן דְּפָסוּל הוּא מָה לִי בְּבַת אַחַת מָה לִי בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues ריש לקיש's statement from step 3, explaining why he calls the answer deceptive: the 'same time' versus 'one after the other' split seems to have no basis.
steps.kashyaTarget: The distinction between slaughtering together and one after the other that רבי עקיבא's answer depends on
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The partner animal is unfit in both cases, so the reason the sprinkling helps it should apply equally to both.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן turns the question back on ריש לקיש with a case of two backup guilt offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש's claim in step 4: don't you also agree there is a difference? He brings a case of two אשמות set aside as a guarantee, where the parts of one were put on the altar before any blood was sprinkled. Wouldn't you agree those parts must come down?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to ריש לקיש: And you, don't you say the same thing? Suppose someone set aside two guilt offerings as backups, slaughtered both, and the כהן went ahead and put the altar-parts of one of them on the altar before any blood was sprinkled. Don't you agree that even though they went up, they must come down?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש's claim that the timing makes no difference, pointing to a ruling ריש לקיש already accepts. This step sets up the case, and the next step shows why it proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of explaining the difference directly, רבי יוחנן brings a case where ריש לקיש agrees to a ruling: parts of a backup אשם put on the altar too early must come down. The key fact to keep in mind is that 'they go up, then they come down.' The next step explains why that ruling only fits if the two animals count as separate.

keyTerms.meaning: Guilt offerings (plural of אָשָׁם).
As a guarantee or backup, so that if one animal is lost, the other can be used.
The parts of an offering that are burned on the altar, like fats and kidneys.
Sprinkling the blood on the altar, the main act that makes the offering work.
'If they went up, they come down.' Even after being placed on the altar, they are taken off.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this line as רבי יוחנן asking for information. 'Don't you say so?' is a debate move: 'You already agree with me.'

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said to Reish Lakish:
And you, do you not say so as well?
Suppose one set aside two guilt offerings as a guarantee,
phrases.notes: He only owes one אשם. The second is a backup in case the first gets lost.

phrases.english: and he slaughtered both of them,

phrases.aramaic: וְקָדַם וְהֶעֱלָה אֵימוּרִין שֶׁל אֶחָד מֵהֶן
phrases.english: and he went ahead and brought up the altar-parts of one of them
before the sprinkling of the blood,

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה מוֹדֶה שֶׁאִם עָלוּ – יֵרְדוּ?
phrases.english: wouldn't you agree that if they went up, they must come down?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's claim in step 4 by pointing to a ruling he himself accepts.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-question from the opponent's own position (a 'you agree too' answer).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that the timing of the slaughter could not matter, since the extra animal is unfit either way.
steps.terutzMaskana: ריש לקיש himself rules that parts of a backup אשם come down from the altar, which will show that the animals can count as separate bodies.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that it makes no difference whether the two animals were slaughtered together or one after the other
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ריש לקיש agrees that the backup אשם's parts come down from the altar. That only makes sense if animals slaughtered one after the other count as separate bodies, so timing does matter.

steps.title: עולא's rule shows the two animals must be separate
steps.stepSummary: If the two animals were one body, the parts should stay on the altar. עולא rules that even parts of קדשים קלים put up before the sprinkling stay up, because they have become the altar's 'bread.' Since here they come down, the animals must count as two separate bodies.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think the two animals are one body, why must the parts come down once they went up? Doesn't עולא say that altar-parts of קדשים קלים that were put up before the blood was sprinkled do not come down, because they have become the altar's bread?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן now explains why the case from step 5 proves his point. He uses עולא's rule to show that the 'they come down' ruling only makes sense if the two animals are separate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא teaches that once parts are on the altar, even too early, they normally stay there. If the backup animal were 'one body' with the animal whose blood was sprinkled, its parts would be tied to a valid offering and should stay up. Since ריש לקיש agrees they come down, he must also hold that this animal stands on its own as a separate, unfit body.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It enters your mind.' If you were to think so.
One body. The two animals would be treated as a single offering.
Offerings of lesser holiness, like a שלמים.
'The bread of the altar.' Once something is on the altar, it now belongs to the altar and stays there.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the proof that whether the animals count as one body or two really matters. It refutes ריש לקיש's claim in step 4 that the timing of the slaughter makes no difference.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ חַד גּוּפָא הוּא,
phrases.english: And if it enters your mind that it is one body,
phrases.notes: He means the two backup animals counting together as one offering.

phrases.english: why, if they went up, must they come down?
But didn't Ulla say:
altar-parts of offerings of lesser holiness

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהֶעֱלָן לִפְנֵי זְרִיקַת דָּם – לֹא יֵרְדוּ,
phrases.english: that one brought up before the sprinkling of the blood do not come down,
since they have become the bread of the altar!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ חַד גּוּפָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the logic behind the case set up in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That the two backup animals can count as two separate bodies, not one.
steps.raayaSupportSource: עולא's rule that parts put on the altar before the sprinkling do not come down, combined with ריש לקיש's agreement that in the backup אשם case they do come down.

steps.title: ריש לקיש is silent and רבי יוחנן declares victory
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש has no answer. רבי יוחנן says he has 'cut off the legs of the child,' meaning he has knocked out the support for ריש לקיש's position.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש was silent. רבי יוחנן said: I have cut off the legs of the child.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש cannot answer, so the argument ends here. רבי יוחנן uses a sharp picture to say that his challenge has removed the basis of ריש לקיש's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Silence in the גמרא means the person has no reply, so רבי יוחנן's proof stands. The line about cutting off the child's legs is a vivid way of saying ריש לקיש's argument can no longer 'stand.'

keyTerms.meaning: He was silent. He had no answer.
'I have cut off the legs of the child.' I have removed the support of his argument.

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש questioned why it matters when the animals were slaughtered. רבי יוחנן showed, using the backup אשם case and עולא's rule, that the two animals can count as separate bodies, and ריש לקיש had no answer.

phrases.english: He was silent.
Rabbi Yochanan said:
I have cut off the legs of the child.
phrases.notes: A picture: without legs, his argument can't stand anymore.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Records that the proof of step 6 went unanswered.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן's proof stands. The two backup animals can count as separate bodies, so the timing of the slaughter does matter.

steps.title: The משנה's opening rule: sprinkling works both ways for most-sacred offerings, only strictly for lesser ones
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states its headline rule. Sprinkling the blood of קדשי קדשים creates both a leniency and a stringency. For קדשים קלים it creates only stringency.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The act of sprinkling the blood of קדשי קדשים has an effect that makes things more lenient and an effect that makes things more strict. For קדשים קלים, all of its effects make things more strict.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a general rule about what happens when the blood of an offering is sprinkled. The details come in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה sorts offerings into two groups, קדשי קדשים and קדשים קלים. For the first group, sprinkling makes some things lighter and some things heavier. For the second group, it only makes things heavier. The next lines explain exactly how.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of a new משנה
The act done with the blood, meaning the sprinkling of the blood on the altar
Offerings of the most sacred order, such as חטאת and אשם
Offerings of lesser sanctity, such as שלמים
To make lenient and to make strict

phrases.english: MISHNA:
There is, in the act of the blood of offerings of the most sacred order,
phrases.notes: "The act of the blood" means sprinkling the blood on the altar.

phrases.english: an effect to be lenient and an effect to be stringent;
but in offerings of lesser sanctity, all of it is to be stringent.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ יֵשׁ מַעֲשֵׂה דָמִים בְּקׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים לְהָקֵל וּלְהַחֲמִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ended with ריש לקיש left without an answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sprinkling the blood of קדשי קדשים has both lenient and strict effects. For קדשים קלים its effects are only strict.

steps.title: The leniency for most-sacred offerings: after sprinkling, the meat is no longer subject to misuse
steps.stepSummary: Before sprinkling, one is liable for מעילה on both the altar portions and the meat of קדשי קדשים. After sprinkling, the meat is released from מעילה, while the altar portions stay subject to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? With קדשי קדשים, before the blood is sprinkled, one is liable for מעילה on the altar portions and on the meat. After the blood is sprinkled, one is still liable for מעילה on the altar portions, but not on the meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה begins explaining its rule by showing the lenient side for קדשי קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before sprinkling, everything about the animal belongs fully to הקדש, so misusing any part is מעילה. Sprinkling the blood permits the meat to the כהנים, so it is no longer treated as הקדש for מעילה. That is the leniency. The altar portions are still meant only for the altar, so they stay subject to מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? The משנה is about to explain its general rule
Sprinkling the blood on the altar
One is liable for מְעִילָה, misuse of consecrated property
The parts of an offering that are burned on the altar

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read "not liable for the meat" as saying the meat is no longer holy. It is still קדשים and may only be eaten by כהנים. It is simply no longer subject to the law of מעילה.

phrases.english: How so?
Offerings of the most sacred order, before the sprinkling of the blood:
one is liable for misuse of their altar portions and of the meat.
After the sprinkling of the blood:
one is liable for misuse of their altar portions,
but one is not liable for misuse of the meat.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד? קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים לִפְנֵי זְרִיקַת דָּמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the lenient half of the קדשי קדשים rule from step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For קדשי קדשים, sprinkling the blood releases the meat from מעילה. The altar portions stay subject to it.

steps.title: The stringency for most-sacred offerings: פיגול, נותר and טומאה apply to both parts
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives the strict side: one is liable for פיגול, נותר and eating while טמא on both the altar portions and the meat. It concludes that sprinkling for קדשי קדשים is both lenient and strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: For both the altar portions and the meat, one is liable for eating פיגול, for eating נותר, and for eating while טמא. So it turns out that the sprinkling of the blood of קדשי קדשים works both to be lenient and to be strict.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה shows the strict side for קדשי קדשים and then sums up the first half of its rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 showed the leniency about the meat. Here the משנה shows that both the meat and the altar portions are covered by the serious prohibitions of פיגול, נותר and טמא, which is the stringency. With both sides shown, the משנה closes the קדשי קדשים half with "נמצא".

keyTerms.meaning: An offering made invalid by an improper intention about when it would be eaten or burned; eating it carries כרת
Sacrificial meat left over past its allowed time
Eating sacrificial meat while ritually impure
It turns out; introduces a summary

steps.whatToRemember: For קדשי קדשים, sprinkling is a mix: the meat leaves מעילה (lenient), and both parts carry פיגול, נותר and טמא (strict).

phrases.english: And for this and for that:
phrases.notes: "This and that" means the altar portions and the meat.

phrases.english: one is liable because of piggul, notar, and impurity.
It turns out that the act of the blood of offerings of the most sacred order
is to be lenient and to be stringent,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל זֶה וְעַל זֶה חַיָּיב מִשּׁוּם פִּיגּוּל נוֹתָר וְטָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the strict side next to the lenient side from step 9, then sums up the קדשי קדשים rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both the altar portions and the meat of קדשי קדשים carry liability for פיגול, נותר and טמא, so sprinkling has both lenient and strict effects.

steps.title: For lesser-sanctity offerings, sprinkling only makes things stricter
steps.stepSummary: For קדשים קלים there is no מעילה at all before sprinkling. After sprinkling, the altar portions become subject to מעילה. The meat never is, so sprinkling only adds stringency.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for קדשים קלים, all of its effects are strict. How so? With קדשים קלים, before the blood is sprinkled, one is not liable for מעילה on the altar portions or on the meat. After the blood is sprinkled, one is liable for מעילה on the altar portions, but not on the meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns to the second half of its rule and explains why sprinkling for קדשים קלים is only strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קדשים קלים are not treated as fully belonging to הקדש for מעילה before sprinkling, so nothing about them carries מעילה. Sprinkling sets the altar portions aside for the altar, and only then does misusing them become מעילה. Since the meat was never subject to מעילה, nothing becomes more lenient. The only change is a new stringency.

keyTerms.meaning: One is not liable for מְעִילָה
All of its effects are to make things stricter

steps.confusionAlert: With קדשי קדשים, sprinkling takes the meat out of מעילה. With קדשים קלים, sprinkling brings the altar portions into מעילה. The same act moves things in opposite directions.
steps.whatToRemember: The two groups mirror each other. Sprinkling releases the meat of קדשי קדשים from מעילה, but it brings the altar portions of קדשים קלים into מעילה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that sprinkling the blood is the key moment that decides which parts of an offering count as belonging to הקדש for the law of מעילה.

phrases.english: But in offerings of lesser sanctity, all of them are to be stringent.
How so?
Offerings of lesser sanctity, before the sprinkling of the blood:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מוֹעֲלִין לֹא בָּאֵימוּרִין וְלֹא בַּבָּשָׂר,
phrases.english: one is not liable for misuse, neither of the altar portions nor of the meat;
after the sprinkling of the blood:
one is liable for misuse of the altar portions,
but one is not liable for misuse of the meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the קדשי קדשים half of the rule in steps 9 and 10 to the קדשים קלים half from step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For קדשים קלים there is no מעילה before sprinkling. After sprinkling, only the altar portions are subject to מעילה, so sprinkling only adds stringency.

steps.title: After sprinkling, קדשים קלים carry פיגול, נותר and טמא, so sprinkling is all stringency
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states that after the sprinkling of the blood of קדשים קלים, one is liable for פיגול, נותר and eating while טמא on both the altar portions and the meat. It concludes that for קדשים קלים, sprinkling only adds stringency.
steps.simpleTranslation: For both this and that, one is liable because of פיגול, נותר and eating while טמא. It turns out that the blood service of קדשים קלים is entirely for stringency.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list of what sprinkling does to קדשים קלים and sums up the whole picture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 showed that sprinkling adds מעילה to the altar portions. Here the משנה adds that sprinkling also makes both the altar portions and the meat subject to פיגול, נותר and טמא. Since nothing becomes more lenient, the summary is 'כולן להחמיר', all for stringency.

keyTerms.meaning: To be strict, to add restrictions

steps.whatToRemember: For קדשי קדשים, sprinkling is both lenient and strict. For קדשים קלים, sprinkling is only strict.

phrases.english: For this and for that
phrases.notes: 'This and that' means the altar portions and the meat.

phrases.english: one is liable for it because of פיגול,
נותר, and eating while impure.
It turns out that the blood service
for offerings of lesser holiness is entirely for stringency.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִמְצָא מַעֲשֵׂה דָמִים בְּקָדָשִׁים קַלִּים כּוּלָּן לְהַחֲמִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes step 11 by adding the strict laws that apply after sprinkling, then sums up the rule for קדשים קלים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After sprinkling, both the altar portions and the meat of קדשים קלים are subject to פיגול, נותר and טמא. So sprinkling for קדשים קלים is entirely stringent.

steps.title: Why would there be any prohibition on meat that belongs to the כהן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the משנה's wording 'אין מועלין בבשר' as hinting that there is still an איסור on the meat of קדשי קדשים after sprinkling. It asks why, since the meat now belongs to the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches: 'One does not commit מעילה with the meat.' So it is מעילה that does not apply, but a prohibition does apply. Why? The meat is the כהן's property!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה and challenges a hidden implication in its wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying only 'there is no מעילה' sounds like something less than 'fully permitted'. That would mean some איסור is left. But after sprinkling, the meat of קדשי קדשים belongs to the כהנים and they may eat it, so a leftover איסור makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Misusing הקדש property for personal benefit
A prohibition (weaker than full מעילה liability)
The property of the כהן

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not asking whether there is מעילה. It agrees there isn't. It is asking why the wording suggests there is still some lesser איסור.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It teaches
"One does not commit misuse with the meat"
It is misuse that does not apply,
but a prohibition does apply.
But why? It is the priest's property!

steps.triggerLanguage: מְעִילָה הוּא דְּלֵיכָּא, הָא אִיסּוּרָא אִיכָּא, וְאַמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis by going back to the wording of step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication of the משנה's phrase 'אין מועלין בבשר' after sprinkling for קדשי קדשים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording implies that some איסור remains. But the meat belongs to the כהן after sprinkling, so no איסור should remain.

steps.title: The wording just matches the first clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה said 'אין מועלין' only to match the phrase 'מועלין' in the רישא. There is no hidden איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Since the first clause used the word 'מועלין', the latter clause used 'אין מועלין'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by explaining that the משנה's wording is a matter of style, not a hidden rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inference in step 13 depended on reading 'there is no מעילה' as precise. The answer is that the משנה chose this phrase to parallel the רישא, which spoke of 'מועלין' before sprinkling. So the meat is fully permitted to the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the question has an answer
The first clause of the משנה
The latter clause of the משנה
Used, took (a phrase)

phrases.english: It is not difficult,
since the first clause used "one commits misuse,"
the latter clause used "one does not commit misuse."

steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the inference from the wording: the phrase was chosen to parallel the רישא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase 'אין מועלין' was precise, implying that some איסור remains on the meat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase just matches the רישא. The meat is fully permitted to the כהנים.

steps.title: Quoting the סיפא about קדשים קלים to raise the same question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the סיפא of the משנה about קדשים קלים, which also uses the phrase 'אין מועלין בבשר'. This sets up the next challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say the latter clause: 'For קדשים קלים, all is for stringency. How so? The meat of קדשים קלים before sprinkling: one does not commit מעילה with them or their altar portions, and one is not liable for them because of פיגול, נותר and טמא. After sprinkling: one commits מעילה with their altar portions, and one does not commit מעילה with the meat.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the end of the משנה again. It is setting up a new challenge on the same phrase 'אין מועלין בבשר' in the סיפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 14 explained 'אין מועלין' as matching an earlier 'מועלין' in the same section. By quoting the סיפא, the גמרא is getting ready to test whether that explanation also works there. The challenge itself comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח
The parts of the animal burned on the מזבח
How so? (introduces details)

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:
"For offerings of lesser holiness, all is for stringency.
How so?

phrases.aramaic: בְּשַׂר קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים לִפְנֵי זְרִיקַת דָּמִים –
phrases.english: The meat of offerings of lesser holiness, before the sprinkling of the blood:
one does not commit misuse with them or with their altar portions,
and one is not liable for them
because of פיגול, נותר, or eating while impure.
After the sprinkling of the blood:
one commits misuse with their altar portions
and one does not commit misuse with the meat."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After answering the question on the רישא, the גמרא turns to the סיפא to test the same answer there.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The סיפא of the משנה: for קדשים קלים there is no מעילה and no פיגול, נותר or טמא before sprinkling. After sprinkling, the altar portions are subject to מעילה but the meat is not.

steps.title: If the meat has no מעילה, is it still forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads 'אין מועלין בבשר' in the סיפא as hinting that the meat of קדשים קלים is still forbidden after sprinkling. It asks why, since the meat belongs to the owners.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is only מעילה that does not apply, which means a prohibition does apply. But why? Isn't the meat the owners' property?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a careful reading of the סיפא's words and then challenges what those words seem to imply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said only that there is no מעילה on the meat, which sounds like there is still some איסור. But after sprinkling, the meat of קדשים קלים belongs to the owners and they may eat it. So the גמרא asks what איסור could possibly remain.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition. Here it means the meat would be forbidden to eat, even with no מעילה.
Property of the owners. After sprinkling, the owners of קדשים קלים may eat the meat.
Why? The word the גמרא uses to open a challenge.

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same kind of question as in Step 13, but it is a different case. There, the meat of קדשי קדשים belongs to the כהנים. Here, the meat of קדשים קלים belongs to the owners. Do not mix up the two answers.

phrases.english: It is only misuse that does not apply,
which implies a prohibition does apply,
But why?
Isn't it the property of the owners!

steps.triggerLanguage: מְעִילָה הוּא דְּלֵיכָּא, הָא אִיסּוּרָא אִיכָּא, וְאַמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the סיפא quoted in Step 15 to raise the challenge that Step 15 was setting up.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implied איסור in the סיפא's words 'אין מועלין בבשר' for קדשים קלים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After sprinkling, the meat of קדשים קלים belongs to the owners and they may eat it, so no איסור should remain.

steps.title: The משנה is talking about meat that went out, and it follows רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא answers that the סיפא is talking about meat that left its permitted area before the sprinkling. That meat really is forbidden, and the משנה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: The משנה is talking about meat that went out, and it follows the view of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא answers the question by saying which case the משנה is about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat of קדשים קלים that left its permitted area before the sprinkling becomes invalid, so it is forbidden to eat. That is the איסור the משנה hints at. The משנה still discusses sprinkling for this meat because, in the earlier משנה, רבי עקיבא holds that sprinkling works even on meat that went out.

keyTerms.meaning: Meat that went out of the area where it may be eaten. Such meat becomes invalid.

steps.whyThisMatters: Unlike Step 14, this answer does not say the wording just copies the רישא. Here the איסור is real, but it comes from the meat leaving its area, not from the sprinkling.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:
It refers to meat that went out,
and it follows Rabbi Akiva.
phrases.notes: This points back to רבי עקיבא's view in the earlier משנה on ו׳ ע״ב: sprinkling works even on meat that went out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: לַיּוֹצְאִין, וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 16 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the משנה is about meat that left its permitted area, following רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to be talking about normal meat of קדשים קלים, which should be fully permitted to the owners.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is talking about meat that went out. That meat is forbidden because it went out, and sprinkling still has an effect according to רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: What רבי עקיבא means by 'sprinkling works' for meat that went out
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא begins to explain רבי עקיבא's view. When רבי עקיבא says sprinkling works on meat that went out, he means it works with regard to that meat's burning. The sentence continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי עקיבא said sprinkling is effective, he meant for meat that went out, with regard to its burning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא starts explaining how far רבי עקיבא's rule goes. This is setup, and the explanation continues in the next lines of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sprinkling cannot make meat that went out permitted to eat. Instead, רבי עקיבא's 'sprinkling works' is about the rules for how and when this meat is burned. Sprinkling gives it the status of meat whose blood was sprinkled, so one waits before burning it rather than burning it right away.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling is effective. Even meat that went out takes on the status of meat whose blood was sprinkled.
Burning. Invalid sacrificial meat must be burned.

steps.confusionAlert: 'Sprinkling works' does not mean the meat that went out becomes permitted to eat. It stays forbidden. Sprinkling only affects its other rules, such as when it is burned.

phrases.english: When Rabbi Akiva said
sprinkling is effective,
for meat that went out, he meant with regard to its burning,

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא זְרִיקָה מוֹעֶלֶת, לַיּוֹצֵא לִשְׂרֵיפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי חנינא's answer from Step 17 by explaining the limits of רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא's rule that sprinkling works on meat that went out applies to the rules of its burning. It does not make the meat permitted to eat.
